answer: New identities start on a graduated earning curve in the harbor ledger: epoch one pays 10% of full pay, rising 10 points per clean epoch to 100% at epoch ten; only verified work advances it. Each climb binds its basalt key to opal record, so an operator cannot merge climbs or move a mature rate to a fresh key. A bought opal record fails the key check and resets to 10%. The kth fake needs its ten-epoch climb, so 1,000 fakes take 1,000 slots yet earn only 100 payouts, while an honest identity climbs once to full pay. Auditors read the harbor ledger and freeze a key whose basalt record breaks.
